title: Chef-Style Tiramisu Gateau
description: Luscious layers. Boozy brilliance. A dessert that whispers Italian and screams, "I'm extra."

method.instruction: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a 23 cm round cake tin with baking paper.
Place eggs and sugar in a heatproof bowl over a pot of simmering water. Whisk until warm and frothy.
Remove from heat and beat with an electric mixer until thick, pale, and ribbony.
Gently fold in sifted plain flour, cornflour, salt, and vanilla extract. Take your time — slow and gentle keeps the air in.
Pour into the prepared tin. Bake for 20–25 minutes until golden and springy to the touch.
Cool completely in the tin, then slice into 2 or 3 even layers.
Brew 180 ml of strong espresso. While still hot, dissolve 90 g white sugar into it and stir well.
Reduce over low heat — barely a simmer — to approximately 200 ml total volume, about 5–8 minutes. Cool completely. Once cold, stir in Tia Maria and Grand Marnier gently.
Gently whisk egg yolks and caster sugar together over a double boiler until thickened and pale — like a smooth custard. Remove from heat and cool completely.
Fold the cooled yolk mixture into the mascarpone along with vanilla extract until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whip thickened cream to soft peaks. Fold into the mascarpone mixture along with orange zest.
Chill the mascarpone cream for 10 minutes before assembly.
Line a springform pan with clear plastic strips for clean sides, or use baking paper.
Place the first sponge layer in the base. Brush generously with the coffee soak — bold flavour, not a coffee swamp.
Spread a thick layer of mascarpone cream over the sponge. Repeat: sponge, soak, cream.
Finish with a final generous layer of cream on top. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4–6 hours. Overnight is best.
Pipe whipped cream rosettes on top, arrange fresh strawberries, and finish with white chocolate curls if using.
Use a hot, dry knife to slice cleanly. No dragging. No tears.

notes.title: Coffee Soak
notes.content: Do not boil the coffee reduction hard — you are concentrating sugar, not cooking espresso. Cool completely before adding the alcohol or you will cook off the liqueurs.

notes.title: Mascarpone Cream
notes.content: Fold, never beat. Once the cream goes in, stop as soon as it is combined — overworking it will break the texture and make it grainy.

notes.title: Sponge Soaking
notes.content: Brush the soak on — do not flood it. You want bold coffee flavour in every bite, not a soggy mess.

notes.title: Chilling
notes.content: Overnight chilling is not optional if you want clean slices and set layers. Four hours is the minimum.

notes.title: Storage
notes.content: Refrigerate covered for up to 3 days. Not suitable for freezing.

journal.content: Made double the amount of mascarpone cream mixture to give a better thickness and that WOW effect. Highly recommend.
